title: One Take, Zoom Levels, Ink, Futures & the Island
description: Continuous shared-element beats, a level-of-detail canvas, strokes clipped to letterforms, speculative drag futures and a spring island.

drops.title: One Take, No Cuts
drops.description: Four beats, one element: each boundary has to name what survives it, or the whole thing is just a slideshow.
drops.concept: onetake's rule is that every beat grows out of the one before, and every boundary names the element that carries across it — a bar collapses into a rail, the rail opens into a window, the window reflows into a phone, the phone converges on the lockup. The demo drives all four beats as a pure function of time off one morphing element, with a camera that leads the subject, whips on the move and rests while holding. The Cut toggle swaps the shared geometry for a dissolve so you can watch the continuity score collapse from 0.83 to 0.00.
drops.source: feitangyuan/onetake — motion films where every beat grows out of the one before

interaction.mouse: Click anywhere on the stage to scrub the timeline
interaction.click: Flip between Carry and Cut, or toggle the labels that name each carried element
interaction.touch: Tap to scrub; panel drops below the stage on small screens

drops.title: Layout That Changes With Zoom
drops.description: Thousands of cards on an infinite canvas: cached thumbnails far out, real typeable DOM once you cross the promote threshold.
drops.concept: gpucanvas keeps thousands of live DOM nodes on a pannable canvas by giving every node a 1/16-scale thumbnail in an atlas layer that is never evicted, then adding sharper rasters as you zoom in. This demo isolates that idea without WebGPU: every node gets one cached thumbnail blitted to a canvas, the viewport culls everything outside it, and only nodes inside the view get promoted to real DOM above the threshold. Pan and zoom only move a transform — they never touch the DOM.
drops.source: berkantay/gpucanvas — live DOM nodes on a GPU-drawn infinite canvas

interaction.mouse: Drag to pan, scroll to zoom toward the cursor; type into any promoted card
interaction.click: Toggle culling, outline the tiles being blitted, or move the promote threshold
interaction.touch: Drag to pan; the zoom slider stands in for pinch

drops.title: Written, Not Revealed
drops.description: A tapered pen stroke clipped to the letter outline, so ink can only ever land inside the glyph.
drops.concept: tegaki animates handwriting from any font by clipping its strokes to the letter outlines rather than authoring paths by hand, with stagger and stroke easing controlling the rhythm and a taper plugin shaping the nib. This demo does exactly that in canvas: each glyph is drawn into an offscreen buffer, a tapered gradient sweep is composited in as destination-in, and the result is stamped back with a glow and a travelling pen tip. Three pens write the same line with different nibs.
drops.source: gkurt/tegaki — handwriting animation for the web, from any font

interaction.mouse: Drag stagger, speed, taper and glow; pick an easing curve
interaction.click: Write it again, or stop the loop on the finished artwork
interaction.touch: Type your own text in the field and it is rewritten immediately

drops.title: Drag Toward What It Could Become
drops.description: The drop zones are not hitboxes — they are rendered futures, read back from a speculative layout of each reachable state.
drops.concept: Dragology's premise is that making something draggable should mean declaring what it can become. The engine speculatively renders each candidate model state, finds where the dragged element lands in every one, and synthesises the drag from those landings. Here the only geometry in the file is one pure layout function: pick a card up and the board lays out four futures, shows where the card would land in each, pulls toward the nearest, and moves the other cards into whichever future you are hovering.
drops.source: declarative-dragging/dragology — declarative dragging for SVG on the web

interaction.mouse: Drag any card; dashed outlines are the rendered futures, green is the one pulling
interaction.click: Toggle the futures and the threads, or retune the snap pull, lift and settle spring
interaction.touch: Full touch dragging with pointer capture

drops.title: Four Shapes, One Island
drops.description: Idle, compact, split and expanded from one black pill that never mounts or unmounts — only the springs move.
drops.concept: islandcn rebuilds Apple's Dynamic Island as an open component, with four presentations and springs fitted frame by frame to recordings of the real thing. This demo keeps the part that matters: one element whose width, height and radius are integrated by an actual spring solver, with the content for each presentation cross-faded on top and nothing ever unmounting. Retune stiffness, damping and mass, watch the settle time change, and flip on reduced motion to see it snap.
drops.source: opencoredev/islandcn — an open-source Dynamic Island for React, installed with shadcn

interaction.mouse: Tap the island to expand it, long-press to dismiss, or start an activity from the buttons
interaction.click: Retune stiffness, damping and mass; toggle reduced motion and the auto demo
interaction.touch: Tap and long-press both work; the island rescales to fit the phone
